mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average for two consecutive months, market expectations of future rate cuts rise, lowering real discount rates and boosting equity present-value pricing, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1-year average(FEDFUNDS) for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the 20-day forward return during the previous 60-day period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 2-month moving average(PAYEMS) AND UNRATE < 2-month moving average(UNRATE)
failure_condition: In 80% of similar labor-market-strong events, the 20-day forward return is non-positive (median negative), or the Sharpe ratio of the 20-day forward return is not significantly higher than the 5-day rolling average (Granger causality fails).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden surge in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) accompanied by rising industrial production (INDPRO) creates a dual positive demand shock that accelerates corporate investment and earnings growth, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 2-week moving average(HOUST) AND INDPRO > 2-week moving average(INDPRO)
failure_condition: Over 10 such demand events, the 5-day forward return is negative in more than 70% of cases, or the event fails to Granger-cause the 5-day realized return (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial supply (INDPRO) below trend suggests production bottlenecks that raise input costs and slow output growth, which compresses equity discounting and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In 50+ supply-contraction episodes, the 20-day forward return is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.10) after controlling for macroeconomic risk factors (Fama-French factors).

mechanism_narrative: When the annualized CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, markets anticipate a sharp policy tightening cycle, raising real rates and depressing equity valuations, which results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: During 10 such inflation spikes, the 60-day forward return is not significantly negative (median ≥ 0.01) after adjusting for macroeconomic risk (Fama-French).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in unemployment (UNRATE) to a new monthly low, without a corresponding rise in labor force participation (PAYEMS), signals a tight labor market that fuels wage growth and consumer spending, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 2-month moving average(UNRATE) AND PAYEMS = 2-month moving average(PAYEMS)
regime_hint: Labor market tightness without participation surge
failure_condition: In 30 such events, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.10) after controlling for sector-specific earnings momentum proxies (e.g., S&P 500 sector beta).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer spending proxies (HOUST) over three consecutive months, despite stable industrial production (INDPRO), suggests a late-cycle slowdown that raises uncertainty and compresses growth expectations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 3-month moving average(HOUST) AND INDPRO > 3-month moving average(INDPRO) for three consecutive months
failure_condition: During 15 such episodes, the 60-day forward return is not significantly negative (median ≥ 0.005) after adjusting for sector-specific risk premia (value vs growth).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly industrial production index (INDPRO) falls below its 12-month moving average for two consecutive months, it indicates a supply-side shock that raises input costs and reduces capacity utilization, which lowers equity discount rates and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average(INDPRO) for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 20 such episodes, the 5-day forward return is not statistically negative (median ≥ 0.002) after controlling for contemporaneous oil price shocks and macroeconomic risk factors.
